title: Holding Complexity Under Pressure: What Your Meeting Transcripts Actually Reveal
summary: Logan Yonavjak spent close to two decades moving capital in impact finance before concluding that the real variable behind every deal was the leader making the decisions, so she co-founded Readiness Engine to measure that directly. Her argument is that leadership capacity is already visible in the way people talk at work, and that quantitative linguistics run over board updates, all hands calls, and internal meetings can score it more consistently than any human reviewer will. She walks through the six constructs the platform measures, the counterintuitive pattern she keeps finding (founders with high relational intelligence who take in every viewpoint and then freeze at the pivot), and why the fix is pairing that founder with a faster mover instead of coaching the trait away. Sales leaders who run weekly coaching calls, anyone making promotion or succession decisions, and founders curious about their own growth edges will get the most out of this one.
keyQuote: Even someone whose job it is to perform a judgment on a case can get tired or grumpy or irritated at different points in the day. You're not necessarily getting the same person consistently.
guestBio: Logan Yonavjak spent close to two decades in impact finance before turning to leadership measurement. She worked at Morgan Stanley, the World Resources Institute, and the Yale Investments Office, and later co-founded Provenance Capital Group, a sell-side advisory firm focused on food and agriculture that directed hundreds of millions of dollars into impact investments. She holds an MBA from the Yale School of Management, a Master of Forestry from the Yale School of the Environment, and a B.A. from UNC Chapel Hill. She is now co-founder and CEO of Readiness Engine, which analyzes real work transcripts and one-way video assessments to score leadership readiness across six dimensions including strategic complexity, resilience under pressure, and coachability.
